verdict.rationale: The MCP authentication docs reference an OAuth-style scope (`context:protected:read`) for reading protected context. Hands-on probes show the hosted MCP sits behind an RFC 9728 OAuth wall with an authorization server, and the CLI uses a device-code login an agent can drive. Together these suggest agents receive scoped tokens, but nothing shows a user deliberately issuing least-privilege credentials for an agent. missing for 10: a documented way to create, scope and revoke agent API keys or tokens, a full scope catalog, least-privilege guidance, and hands-on evidence of a scoped grant. [2026-10-14 re-judge parity audit (owner-product lane): partial 3 -> none 0, restoring both audits on unchanged evidence: one scope name in the MCP auth docs is not an issuance capability, nothing shows a user issuing, configuring or revoking a scoped credential, and every peer sits at none/na on the same absence. Ultrametric-affiliation governance, README §9.]
